audit.why: Content win and full phases[].side are identical — Skill / Urgot / Urgot / Urgot / Urgot / Urgot / Skill — and that matches the data: Trundle loses this lane at 48.70% over 154 games. The only friction is phases[0].why claiming Chomp "wins almost every level-1 exchange" under a Skill label, which is a template line rather than a contradiction worth spending a chart edit on. I left the chart alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page names four spikes and none of them is the one that actually decides the lane: Purge's cooldown and cost fall to nothing as it ranks up — 12/9/6/3/0 seconds and 40/30/20/10/0 mana.
audit.why: At rank 1 Purge is a 12-second, 40-mana commitment and Trundle can trade between casts. At rank 5 it is free and has no cooldown at all, which means the entire 'wait for his cooldown, then fight' plan stops existing partway through the laning phase. Every field on the page tells the player to trade around Disdain; the ability that quietly removes his downtime is never mentioned.
audit.corrected: Front-load the lane while Purge still costs him mana and time. Once it is maxed, Disdain at 16-14s is the only cooldown left to punish.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields build the late game on Urgot dealing percent-health damage: spikes[3] "percent-max-HP shotgun legs ... negates your resistance gains from Subjugate", wants.foe[1] "Stack percent-max-HP damage from W shotgun legs to bypass the armor and MR you steal", whys[6] "starts to bypass the resistance gains Subjugate gave you", and `late` "percent-current-HP damage" — which is not even the same claim as the other three.
audit.why: Riot's own text for Echoing Flames says his legs deal physical damage, and no ability in champ-data/_kits/urgot.json carries a percentHealth flag. _missing-interactions.json raises resistances-invalidated against Zac, Ziggs, Warwick and Zaahen in this same slice and does not raise it against Urgot. So the resistances Subjugate moves from him to you work at both ends: he loses armour, you gain it, and his physical damage is cut twice. The page tells the player his best ultimate stops mattering after two items, which is the opposite of true and changes whether he takes the side-lane duel at all.
audit.corrected: Echoing Flames is physical damage. The armour Subjugate moves across cuts it — what actually beats you late is Purge having no cooldown, not armour penetration.

audit.whatIsWrong: `mid` says Pillar of Ice's "knock-up and slow buys you time to walk back onto W". wants.you[0] and `early` say Chomp slows his attack speed.
audit.why: Pillar of Ice creates impassable terrain and slows nearby enemies — there is no knock-up in it, so a player expecting Urgot to be interrupted by the cast will keep walking into a Purge that never stopped. Chomp's slow is a movement slow and its debuff is an Attack Damage sap; it changes how hard his autos hit, not how fast.
audit.corrected: Pillar of Ice: terrain plus a slow. Chomp: damage, movement slow, AD sap.

audit.whatIsWrong: Disdain is named in fourteen fields as "his engage" or "the flip" and its two decisive properties are never stated: it shields him, and it is his only dash.
audit.why: Riot's text gives Disdain a self-shield on the charge, which is why trading into the flip feels worse than the damage numbers suggest, and it is 16/15.5/15/14.5/14 seconds. That single cooldown is both his gap-closer and his way out, so a flip you survive is a free trade for the next fourteen-plus seconds — the page says "bait it, then duel" without ever telling the player how long the reward lasts.
audit.corrected: Disdain: 16s at rank 1, 475 range, shields him on the charge, and it is his only dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect confirmed: no cooldown number appears in either layer. breakdown.cooldowns lists Disdain twice with no figure, and report[9] says "Commit on Disdain (Flip)'s cooldown" without one.
audit.why: The numbers make the rule: Disdain 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s, Purge 12/9/6/3/0s, Corrosive Charge 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s, Fear Beyond Death 100/85/70s, against Chomp's flat 3.5s. Between two Disdains you get four bites. And Fear Beyond Death at 100 seconds is exactly the window in which Subjugate, at 120 seconds, is the ultimate that is more often down.
audit.corrected: Added figures to breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.mid, report[5], dosFull[0], phases[2] and phases[4].

audit.why: No Urgot ability carries a heal flag, so the absence of anti-heal from report[8] is right, and Plated Steelcaps against a physical-damage kit is right. I left itemization alone.

The packet's suspectName "Use Pillar of Ice" in `mid` is a false positive on the name. Two derived-flag misfires in champ-data/_kits/urgot.json are worth knowing about and I did not write either into the page: Corrosive Charge carries a dash flag despite Riot's text describing a charge fired at a target location, and Disdain carries a projectile flag despite being a body charge.

edits.after: Chomp on Urgot's every last-hit attempt saps his AD before Purge is cheap enough to spam — his W is 12s and 40 mana at rank 1, so levels 1-2 are yours.

edits.after: Disdain rips you out of Frozen Domain and shields him on the charge — it is 16s at rank 1 and his only dash, so every trade you force is timed off that one cooldown.

edits.after: Land Chomp on Urgot's every auto attempt — it saps the AD that Purge and Echoing Flames both scale from, and it is back every 3.5 seconds

edits.before: Chomp on his first auto attempt is the correct level-1 opener — the AD steal and attack-speed slow immediately blunt Urgot's shotgun-legs damage, which requires him to auto you for his W procs to stack. The problem surfaces at level 2: Urgot's Disdain flip can hurl you backward before Frozen Domain is even placed, so drop W at your feet the moment you hit level 2 and position so a potential flip lands you back inside the zone or onto the side of it. His percent-max-HP W damage means he does not need to out-AD you to win trades; you need your domain active to out-heal his sustained poke.
edits.after: Chomp on his first auto attempt is the correct level-1 opener — the AD sap blunts Purge and Echoing Flames together, because both scale off the damage those autos carry. The problem surfaces at level 2: Disdain can hurl you backward before Frozen Domain is even placed, so drop W at your feet the moment you hit 2 and stand so a flip lands you back inside the zone or on its edge. Disdain is 16s at rank 1 and shields him as he charges, so it is his opener as much as his exit. Purge costs 40 mana on 12s at rank 1 — that is the window where his poke is genuinely limited, and the one you have to cash.

edits.before: This is where the matchup becomes a genuine chess game. Urgot's E flip is his primary tool for voiding your Frozen Domain — if he flips you away from it, you lose the movement speed to re-engage and the healing that keeps you alive, and suddenly his shotgun-legs proc DPS overtakes yours. Use Pillar of Ice reactively behind him after the flip so he cannot chase you off; the knock-up and slow buys you time to walk back onto W. At level 6, Subjugate is your biggest equalizer: open every all-in with R to drain his armor before your Chomp autos land, and keep him on the outer edge of your W so the terrain created by Pillar blocks his disengage toward his tower.
edits.after: This is where the matchup becomes a genuine chess game. Disdain is his tool for voiding your Frozen Domain — flipped off the zone you lose the move speed to re-engage and the healing that keeps you alive, and his Purge volleys start winning. Use Pillar of Ice reactively behind him after the flip: it is terrain plus a slow, and the walk-around it forces is what buys the seconds to get back onto W. Disdain is 16s at rank 1, so a flip you survive is a free trade. At level 6, Subjugate is your equaliser: open every all-in with R so 40% of his armour and a fifth of his health move across before your Chomp autos land, and keep the Pillar between him and his tower.

edits.before: Neither side dominates the 2-plus-item game cleanly — which is exactly what 48.7% looks like. Urgot's Heartsteel stacking and percent-current-HP damage begin to outpace the raw resistances you drain with Subjugate; he hurts you proportionally regardless of how much armor you have. Your plan is to be the better teamfight Subjugate target elsewhere: if their team runs a bigger tank than Urgot, use R on them instead and let Urgot be a split-push problem your team collapses on. In a straight side-lane duel at full items, always R first, Pillar his escape route, and do not let the fight extend long enough for two full execute-threshold windows on his R.
edits.after: Neither side dominates the 2-plus-item game cleanly — which is exactly what 48.7% looks like. Urgot's Heartsteel stacking makes him hard to finish, but Echoing Flames is physical damage, so the armour Subjugate moves from him to you cuts it at both ends. What actually beats you is Purge: at rank 5 it costs no mana and has no cooldown, so he gets to lengthen every trade for free. Be the better teamfight Subjugate target elsewhere — if their team runs a bigger tank than Urgot, R them instead and let Urgot be a split-push problem your team collapses on. In a duel at full items, R first, Pillar his path home, and never let the fight run into a second Fear Beyond Death at 70 seconds.

edits.before: Urgot can W-proc you from outside your comfort range; Q Chomp is on a short cooldown but his legs activate passively, so extended four-to-five second trades are coin-flip territory without your W active.
edits.after: Urgot can Purge you from 490 range and Echoing Flames triggers off it, so four-to-five second trades are coin-flip territory without your W down. His W cost falls every rank too — 40 mana at 1, nothing at 5.

edits.before: At two-plus items Urgot's percent-max-HP shotgun damage scales with his HP stacking and starts to bypass the resistance gains Subjugate gave you — do not look for the straight duel; play for teamfight Subjugate value on their bigger tanks.
edits.after: At two-plus items Urgot's health stacking makes him hard to finish, but Echoing Flames is physical and the armour Subjugate moves onto you still cuts it. The real reason to skip the duel is Purge: at rank 5 it costs nothing and has no cooldown at all.

edits.after: His W shreds and pokes — dodge his flip, duel him in your W. Disdain is 16s at rank 1 and Purge is free at rank 5, so take your fights while his W still costs him something.

notes: The 'Urgot deals percent-max-HP damage' claim is load-bearing on this page — it is the stated reason Subjugate stops working after two items — and nothing in Riot's text or the derived flags supports it. The same phrasing appears as 'percent-current-HP' in `late`, which is a second, incompatible version of the same claim, so at least one of them was invented. Worth sweeping every Urgot entry in every champion's file for it. Two derived-flag misfires in champ-data/_kits/urgot.json: Corrosive Charge is flagged as a dash and Disdain as a projectile; both contradict Riot's descriptions and I trusted the descriptions. Chart left alone — content and full agree and both match the 48.70% data.
